description:
Income, poverty and employment: median household income and per capita income ([B19013](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013), [B19301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19301)), the share of people below the poverty line and below twice it ([C17002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.C17002)), the share of households receiving SNAP ([B22010](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B22010)), the unemployment rate as a share of the civilian labor force ([B23025](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B23025)), the household income distribution collapsed to 7 shares from under $25,000 to $200,000 or more ([B19001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19001)), and median earnings for workers with earnings ([B20002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B20002)) — plus, at every level but block groups, where the Census Bureau does not publish them, the Gini index of income inequality ([B19083](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19083)) and the poverty rate by age for children under 18 and adults 65 and over ([B17001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B17001)), plus total population ([B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003)) and population density for context.

Curated indicators for all **441** congressional districts of the 119th Congress in the United States, Puerto Rico and the island areas, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs.html) **2020–2024 5-year estimates** (`acsdt5y2024`, the table-based [Summary File](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/)). The Census Bureau calls the ACS "the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing". The Bureau also publishes 1-year estimates at this geography; the 5-year release is used throughout this catalog so every geography in it is the same vintage and directly comparable.

Every estimate ships with its margin of error — `<column>_moe`, at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes — and the headline statistics also carry a coefficient of variation (`<column>_cv` = `moe / 1.645 / estimate`) so small-area noise can be flagged rather than mapped as if certain. Derived percentages propagate error with the Census Bureau's own formulas from [ACS Accuracy of the Data](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/MultiyearACSAccuracyofData2024.pdf): sums add in quadrature, proportions use the subset formula with the ratio formula as fallback. ACS jam values for suppressed or unestimable cells are NULL here, never numbers, and medians are published as the Bureau publishes them — a median cannot be aggregated to a larger area. Each column's description names its ACS table, its exact universe, and the lines summed to make it.

Districts are equal-population by construction — 546,488 to 1,021,191 people across the 435 voting districts, 771,301 at the median of all 437 rows with data (measured) — so the distribution of every rate here is far tighter than at any other geography, and the map styles' class breaks are measured accordingly. These are the districts of the **119th Congress** ([the vintage this ACS release tabulates](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/geography-acs/geography-boundaries-by-year/2024.html)); district numbers are not stable across congresses, so do not join these GEOIDs to an earlier congress's districts of the same number. Nothing is suppressed beyond the four island-area delegate districts: `median_hh_income` is published for 437 of the 441 rows, with a median coefficient of variation of **0.010** (measured).

Geometries are the Census Bureau's [2024 cartographic boundary files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for congressional districts of the 119th Congress (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), reprojected to EPSG:4326 and joined on `GEOID`. Cartographic rather than TIGER/Line because TIGER extends census geographies into open water while the cartographic files clip to the shoreline, which is what a choropleth wants. The file is `cb_2024_us_cd119_500k` — `CDSESSN = '119'` on all 441 features — matching the congress this release tabulates.

The join is driven by geometry, so a geography with 2024 boundaries but no ACS tabulation keeps its row with NULL values instead of disappearing: 4 delegate districts (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands) in the island areas, which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates because the Island Areas run a separate decennial-only program. In the other direction, three ACS district rows have no polygon and so no row here: `09ZZ`, `17ZZ` and `33ZZ`, the water-only pseudo-districts Connecticut, Illinois and New Hampshire contribute to the tabulation, each with population 0. Keeping these rows means a national map has no holes and a consumer can see the absence; dropping them would make "every US geography" quietly mean something narrower.

This is one themed chunk of five at this geography. The other themes are [People & Education](../cd-people/collection.json), [Housing & Rent](../cd-housing/collection.json), [Commuting & Connectivity](../cd-connectivity/collection.json) and [Health, Disability & Income by Race](../cd-wellbeing/collection.json), split that way so a consumer who wants one theme reads one file. Chunks at the same geography hold the same rows and the same geometry, so they join 1:1 on `geoid`. A sixth collection, [All Indicators](../congressional-districts/collection.json), carries all 135 columns on the same rows in one wide table — at this many features width costs little, so take that one if a question crosses themes. A district nests in a state, so `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` reaches the state row; nothing finer joins by prefix, because district boundaries follow 2020 census blocks rather than counties or tracts. Every other geography in this catalog is organized the same way — [block groups](../../block-groups/catalog.json), [census tracts](../../tracts/catalog.json), [counties](../../counties/catalog.json), [states](../../states/catalog.json), [ZCTAs](../../zctas/catalog.json) and [places and CDPs](../../places/catalog.json) — and the [blocks](../../blocks/collection.json) collection carries 2020 Decennial counts, a different survey and vintage rather than a finer version of these numbers.

The PMTiles archive carries the same columns as the GeoParquet, minus the `*_moe` columns, and at every zoom the tiles are the real census geographies — there are few enough features here to draw them all at a national zoom, so this archive needs none of the coarser-geography coarse-zoom bands the catalog's finer collections carry. Built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo). Statistics still come from the GeoParquet: margins of error are not in the tiles.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

doc-acs-handbook.title: Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data — Census Bureau handbooks
doc-acs-handbook.description: The Bureau's own guidance on what ACS estimates can and cannot support: 1-year versus 5-year releases, margins of error, comparing across vintages, and small-area reliability. Read it before drawing a conclusion from a single block group.

doc-acs-accuracy.title: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2024, multiyear estimates)
doc-acs-accuracy.description: The source of every margin-of-error formula this build applies: quadrature for sums, the proportion formula and its ratio fallback for percentages, and the definition of the published 90% confidence level.

doc-acs-subject-definitions.title: ACS 2024 Subject Definitions
doc-acs-subject-definitions.description: The Census Bureau's definitions of the concepts behind these columns — household, householder, gross rent, poverty status determined, group quarters, means of transportation to work, disability. Where a column description here says what a universe is, this is the document it is saying it from.

doc-geo-glossary.title: Census Bureau geography program glossary
doc-geo-glossary.description: Definitions of the geographies and the identifiers used here — block, block group, tract, county equivalent, GEOID, and what nests inside what.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 4-character congressional district GEOID — state FIPS (2) + district (2), e.g. `0612` for California's 12th. `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` is the state FIPS code. At-large states use district `00` (AK, DE, ND, SD, VT, WY) and the non-voting delegate districts use `98` (`1198` District of Columbia, `7298` Puerto Rico, plus the four island areas). Districts of the **119th Congress**, which is the vintage the ACS 2020–2024 5-year release tabulates: matches `GEOID` in the `cb_2024_us_cd119_500k` cartographic boundary file (`CDSESSN = '119'` on every feature) and the ACS `5001900US` prefix, whose `19` is the congress number, is stripped. District numbers are not stable across congresses, so a `geoid` here does not join to a 118th-Congress district of the same number.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: `NAMELSAD` from the cartographic boundary congressional district file plus the state name from the state file — "Congressional District 12, California", "Delegate District (at Large), District of Columbia".

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state or territory code (`MO`, `PR`, `GU`). Carried on every collection from the `STATEFP → USPS` lookup embedded in `tools/specs.py` rather than read off the boundary files, because the 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file has no `STUSPS` column while the tract, county and state files do.

table:columns.name: population
table:columns.description: Total population. Universe: total population. The single line of [B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003) (Total Population), published as an integer. Carried on every ACS collection so a rate can be weighted or sanity-checked without a second download. NULL on 0.91% of districts — the four island-area delegate districts (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands), which have 2024 boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates. Every other column in this collection is NULL on the same four rows and nowhere else.

table:columns.name: population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `population` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND / 1e6` from the cartographic boundary file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: pop_density
table:columns.description: People per square kilometre of land area, rounded to 1 decimal: `population / aland_sqkm`. NULL where `ALAND` is 0 or `population` is NULL.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income
table:columns.description: Median household income in the past 12 months, in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars. Universe: households. Line 1 of [B19013](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013), published as the Census Bureau publishes it. A median cannot be aggregated: there is no way to combine the medians of two block groups into the median of their union.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_hh_income` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `median_hh_income`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: per_capita_income
table:columns.description: Per capita income in the past 12 months, in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars — aggregate income divided by total population, so children and people with no income are in the denominator. Universe: total population. Line 1 of [B19301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19301).

table:columns.name: per_capita_income_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `per_capita_income` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty
table:columns.description: Percent of the population below the federal poverty level — an income-to-poverty ratio under 1.00. Universe: population for whom poverty status is determined, which excludes institutionalized people, people in military group quarters and in college dormitories, and unrelated individuals under 15. Lines 2 ("Under .50") + 3 (".50 to .99") of [C17002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.C17002) over line 1.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_below_poverty` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `pct_below_poverty`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_below_2x_poverty
table:columns.description: Percent of the population with an income-to-poverty ratio under 2.00 — a common proxy for low income rather than deep poverty. Universe: population for whom poverty status is determined. Lines 2–7 of [C17002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.C17002) over line 1 (equivalently, everyone not in line 8, "2.00 and over").

table:columns.name: pct_below_2x_poverty_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_below_2x_poverty` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_snap
table:columns.description: Percent of households that received Food Stamps/SNAP benefits at any time in the past 12 months. Universe: households. Line 2 of [B22010](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B22010) over line 1. Receipt by the household, not by individuals, and not a measure of current enrollment.

table:columns.name: pct_snap_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_snap` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_unemployed
table:columns.description: Unemployment rate: unemployed people as a percent of the civilian labor force. Universe for the table is the population 16 years and over, but the denominator here is line 3, "Civilian labor force" — the labor force, not the whole population 16+, because that is what an unemployment rate divides by. Line 5 ("Unemployed") over line 3 of [B23025](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B23025). Members of the Armed Forces and people not in the labor force are excluded from both parts.

table:columns.name: pct_unemployed_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_unemployed` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_income_under_25k
table:columns.description: Percent of households with income under $25,000 in the past 12 months. Universe: households. Lines 2–5 ("Less than $10,000" through "$20,000 to $24,999") of [B19001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19001) (Household Income in the Past 12 Months) over line 1 — the first of 7 shares this catalog collapses B19001's 16 published brackets into.

table:columns.name: pct_income_under_25k_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_income_under_25k` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: median_earnings
table:columns.description: Median earnings in the past 12 months, in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars — wages, salary, and self-employment income, for people who have earnings. Universe: population 16 years and over with earnings in the past 12 months — a narrower universe than `median_hh_income`'s (households) or `per_capita_income`'s (total population): someone with no earnings, retired or unemployed, is outside it, so this is not comparable to either. Line 1 of [B20002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B20002) (Median Earnings in the Past 12 Months by Sex for the Population 16 Years and Over With Earnings), the combined-sex total; the male and female medians the table also publishes are not carried here.

table:columns.name: median_earnings_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_earnings` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: median_earnings_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `median_earnings`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: gini_index
table:columns.description: Gini index of income inequality among households, from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality) — the Census Bureau's own summary statistic, not computed here from the income distribution. Universe: households. The single line of [B19083](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19083) (Gini Index of Income Inequality), published as the Census Bureau publishes it, to 4 decimal places. **Not published for block groups** — B19083 carries no block-group rows in this release (measured against the cached `.dat` file), which is why there is no `gini_index` column in `bg-income`; see that collection's known issues.

table:columns.name: gini_index_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `gini_index` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty_under_18
table:columns.description: Child poverty rate: percent of the population under 18 below the federal poverty level. Universe: population under 18 for whom poverty status is determined — narrower than `pct_below_poverty`'s all-ages universe, so the two percentages are not directly comparable. [B17001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B17001) (Poverty Status in the Past 12 Months by Sex by Age) bins ages non-standardly; the six under-18 age labels ("Under 5 years" through "16 and 17 years") each appear once under the below-poverty branch and once under the at-or-above branch, for each sex. The numerator sums the 12 below-poverty lines for those labels (lines 4–9 male, 18–23 female); the denominator adds the matching 12 at-or-above lines (33–38 male, 47–52 female) to get the full under-18 population for whom poverty status is determined. **Not published for block groups** — B17001 carries no block-group rows in this release (measured); see `bg-income`'s known issues.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty_65_plus
table:columns.description: Senior poverty rate: percent of the population 65 and over below the federal poverty level. Universe: population 65 and over for whom poverty status is determined. The two 65-and-over age labels of [B17001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B17001) ("65 to 74 years", "75 years and over") each appear once under the below-poverty branch and once under the at-or-above branch, for each sex. The numerator sums the 4 below-poverty lines for those labels (15, 16, 29, 30); the denominator adds the matching at-or-above lines (44, 45, 58, 59) to get the full 65-and-over population for whom poverty status is determined. **Not published for block groups** — B17001 carries no block-group rows in this release (measured); see `bg-income`'s known issues.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary congressional district file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the congressional district into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.
